guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard / Fender Telecaster / Danelectro
guitar.evidence: Jimmy Page's 1959 Gibson Les Paul ('Number One') is one of the most iconic guitars in rock history, alongside his well-documented use of a Telecaster (Stairway to Heaven solo) and Danelectro for alternate tunings.

tone.target: dry layered hard-rock crunch with upper-mid bite and sustain
tone.profile: dry layered hard-rock crunch with upper-mid bite and sustain
tone.summary: A tight signal chain utilizing a British preamp (UK 45) for classic crunch, followed by minimal compression and a powerful cabinet simulation to achieve the desired dry, biting hard rock sound.
corrections: favor classic dry Marshall over modern high-gain

rig.name: Led Zeppelin - Achilles Last Stand - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise inherent in high-gain hard rock playing.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for aggressive tones.

blocks.purpose: Smooth out the attack and enhance sustain, providing a solid foundation for the crunch.
blocks.gap: The Comp module is ideal for adding smooth sustain without sounding overly processed, matching the 'smooth sustain' requirement.

blocks.purpose: Provide the core 'tight Marshall crunch' and upper-mid bite required for hard rock.
blocks.gap: The general Distortion model is chosen to emulate a classic Plexi/Marshall tone, avoiding modern fuzz or scooped sounds.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic British Marshall/Plexi stack tone, providing the necessary upper-mid bite and crunch.
blocks.gap: None. This is the definitive choice for classic hard rock tones.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British cabinet sound and necessary upper-mid punch for layered guitars.
blocks.gap: None. Matches the '4x12 cab' clue and dry, direct feel requirement.

blocks.purpose: Boost the upper-mids and treble frequencies to achieve the required 'bright upper-mid bite' without sounding harsh.
blocks.gap: None. Used for surgical tone shaping after the main gain stages.

blocks.purpose: Disabled as per the 'avoid' list and corrections.
blocks.gap: The module is present but explicitly bypassed to meet the tone requirements.

blocks.purpose: Add minimal, subtle echo to enhance the sense of space and sustain without becoming distracting.
blocks.gap: The delay is kept very low (low feedback/mix) to satisfy the 'minimal ambience' requirement.

blocks.purpose: Provide a very subtle, dry room ambience to glue the layered guitars together without sounding wet or cavernous.
blocks.gap: The mix is kept extremely low (20%) to ensure the tone remains 'dry' and direct.

blocks.purpose: Final output level adjustment to match the desired performance volume.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better cabinet realism and upper-mid definition.

proposals.reason: Enhance the vintage British cab sound and bite for layered hard rock.
